Secondly, availability heuristic makes individuals rely on easily accessible examples or memories when forming judgments. This can skew understanding, as it doesn't necessarily reflect the true likelihood or complexity of a situation.

Thirdly, cognitive dissonance creates mental discomfort when new information contradicts existing beliefs, leading to rationalization or denial. This can prevent individuals from updating their knowledge or adapting to new realities.

Lastly, stereotypes and prejudice can shape how we perceive and interpret information about certain groups or topics, leading to unfair generalizations and hindering a comprehensive understanding.

In summary, biases can limit our objectivity, narrow our perspective, and distort our understanding of the world
